p-portal: In CSP you pay for every license purchased, whether it's assigned or not. Finding the ones nobody uses is immediate savings, and the portal flags them.
p-failover: A Site Recovery test failover brings up the replicas in an isolated network: you test the plan without interrupting replication or touching production.
A Site Recovery recovery plan groups the servers and defines the order in which they come up: for example, the database before the application.
p-auditoria: Legacy authentication doesn't support MFA. That's why blocking it is one of the first controls in any identity audit.
Conditional Access has a report-only mode: it lets you measure the impact of a policy before turning it on.
p-gobernanza: An Azure Policy with the Deny effect stops the resource before it is created; with Audit it only flags it. Choosing between the two is a business decision.
With the DeployIfNotExists effect, an Azure Policy can create what's missing (for example, the diagnostic settings) instead of just warning.
p-drlive: Putting a cost per minute on the outage turns the RTO into a number that leadership understands without explaining acronyms.
p-backups: Azure Backup instant restore snapshots are billed separately from the vault: retaining them for too long raises the cost without speeding up recovery much.
Geo-redundant vault storage costs more than local redundancy, but it's the one that lets you restore in another region.
Reassigning a VM to another policy in the same vault keeps its recovery points. Moving it to another vault means protecting it again and paying twice while the old retention lasts.
p-aienv: A language model can give two different answers to the same instruction. That's why ai-env validates every output before running anything.
stack: AZ-305 and AZ-400 are Expert-level certifications: to earn them you first need an Associate-level one.
experiencias: At the buildathon, the rules engine sent each expense down one of three paths: approved, blocked or sent for human review.
comunidad: A backup that was never restored has no known RTO, only an estimate. The featured article is about that gap.
The webinar showed a real recovery test from end to end, with the cost of the outage running on screen.
